SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - FICTIONAL PATIENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
COLONOSCOPY REPORT
Facility: Northgate Ambulatory Endoscopy (fictional)
Patient: Delia Farrow (fictional)
Date of service: November 5, 2026
Endoscopist: Samuel Achterberg, MD (fictional)
Indication: Iron deficiency anemia and intermittent rectal bleeding.
Procedure: The colonoscope was advanced to the cecum; the appendiceal orifice was identified.
Findings:
- Sigmoid colon at 30 cm: two separate lesions lie side by side, about 1 cm apart.
- Lesion A: an 8 mm sessile polyp, removed completely with a cold snare and retrieved.
- Lesion B: a 20 mm firm, ulcerated mass with irregular margins, suspicious for malignancy.
- Lesion B was biopsied with cold forceps (six samples) and was left in place, not removed.
- Scattered sigmoid diverticula. The rest of the colon was normal.
Impression:
1. Lesion A: 8 mm sigmoid polyp, removed by cold snare.
2. Lesion B: 20 mm sigmoid mass suspicious for malignancy, biopsied and left in place.
3. Sigmoid diverticulosis.
Plan: Await pathology; refer to colorectal surgery.
